metaDescription: Corded upright vacuums under $100 compared by weight, dust cup size, brush roll and filter care, so you know what a budget upright does well and what it skips.
expertTake: The Eureka PowerSpeed NEU182B is the best upright under $100 because it pairs a 2.6 liter cup with a light 10 pound body and five height settings. The Eureka Airspeed NEU10AE4 is the pick if weight matters most. Skip this price band for thick wall-to-wall carpet or serious allergies; budget uprights are light cleaners with basic filters.
introParagraphs: At the lowest price band an upright is a simple machine: a plastic body, a belt-driven roll, a bagless cup and a basic filter. It can handle weekly cleaning on low and medium pile and hard floors, and it is a good second vacuum for a flat or a spare room.

What you give up is the stuff that costs money: sealed filtration, a pod, a roll that adapts and a long run of replacement parts. The cap of $100 reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, and prices move, so check the current figure before you buy.

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU182B, 10 lb, 2.6L dust cup

specList.label: Floors
specList.value: Carpet, shag rug and hard floors

products.description:
The NEU182B pairs a light 10 pound body with a 2.6 liter dust cup, which is big for a budget upright and means fewer trips to the bin. Five height adjustments let you set the head for carpet, shag or bare floor, and the maker says the dynamic motor and brush roll lift stubborn debris. Smooth wheels help it glide.

It is the older sibling of the NEU280 and lacks that model's cyclone upgrade, but the cup is larger and the price band is the same. Next to the Airspeed it is heavier and more capable, which suits a house with carpet.

Tip the cup out at the line, rinse the filter monthly and let it dry for a full day. Set the height whenever you change surfaces, since a head too low drags on a rug and a head too high leaves dirt, and check the roll for hair every few weeks. Because the body is plastic, avoid pulling the machine by the cord and lift it over thresholds. The large cup also makes a heavy load when it is full of sand or garden soil, so tip it out at about two thirds and hold the bag close to the opening. On a shag rug raise the height setting one notch so the roll does not bog down, and if the motor note drops, stop and look for a wound strand before you push on, since a stalled roll heats the belt in seconds.
products.bestFor: A first upright for a small house with carpet and hard floor.
pros: 2.6 liter dust cup is large for the price

products.name: Eureka PowerSpeed NEU280 with upgraded cyclone

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Pet hair, carpet and hard floor

products.description:
The NEU280 is the PowerSpeed with a new cyclone system that the maker says handles larger debris such as cereal and cat litter, which earlier budget models struggled with. It stays lightweight and aims to penetrate carpet to lift embedded dirt.

Next to the NEU182B it is a newer design with the cyclone upgrade, while the older model has the larger cup. If your floors see chunky debris, the upgrade is the reason to prefer this one.

Clear the cup well ahead of a full load and rinse the filter monthly. A cyclone design works best when the dirt it separates does not pack against the filter, so do not wait until the cup is full. Check the roll for hair, and wipe the sole plate with a dry cloth every month. Chunky debris is also hard on the roll bearings and the belt, so avoid running it over coins, screws and small toys, which can lodge in the nozzle and jam the roll before the cyclone ever gets a chance to separate them. If you hear a rattle, switch off, unplug and look under the roll cover, since a stuck pebble is far more common than a motor fault and the fix takes a minute with a screwdriver.
products.bestFor: Homes with chunky debris and a pet that want a light upright.

products.name: Eureka Airspeed NEU10AE4, 7.7 lb, quick-release handle
products.description:
At about 7.7 pounds the Airspeed is the lightest upright in the guide. A quick-release handle converts it for above-floor cleaning with a crevice tool or dusting brush, and the compact body stores in a small space.

It is a modest machine, so thick carpet and a large home are beyond it, but for a flat or a bedroom it is easy to carry and easy to use. Next to the NEU182B it has a smaller cup and less capacity.

Empty the small cup after every use, rinse the filter monthly and check the roll for hair. Park it standing against a wall, because a very light body tips easily, and lift the head over rug edges instead of dragging it. With so little weight pressing the head into the carpet the machine relies on the roll for agitation, so go slowly over rugs and make overlapping passes rather than quick strokes. It is a natural second vacuum for a bedroom or a hall, where its low weight is the whole point, and a household that already owns a stronger machine downstairs will often find this is the one that actually gets used every week.
products.bestFor: Small flats and users who need the lightest machine.

products.name: Bissell CleanView Compact 3508, under 8 lb, extension wand
products.description:
The CleanView Compact weighs under eight pounds and carries an extension wand, which makes it the compact choice with reach. A scatter-free feature aims to capture messes on hard floors without pushing them ahead of the brush.

It is built for apartments and dorms, so storage is easy, but the tank is small. Next to the Airspeed it has a wand and a better hard floor design.

Empty the tank after each session, rinse the filter monthly and check the roll for hair. A compact machine tips easily, so park it against a wall corner. Use the wand with one hand on the body so the machine does not slide away, and open the suction control or switch to the wand setting before you put the tool on a curtain, since full suction pulls fabric into the nozzle. The scatter-free feature only helps if you move at a steady pace, so avoid quick back-and-forth strokes on bare floors and let the head glide slowly through crumbs.
products.bestFor: Apartments and dorms with a mix of hard floor and low rugs.

products.name: Dirt Devil Endura Lite upright, multi-floor roll, 6 ft wand
products.description:
The Endura Lite is a lightweight, compact upright with a multi-floor brush roll and a quick-release wand with 6 feet of reach. That wand makes it useful for cobwebs, curtains and the tops of door frames.

It is a plain machine with a plastic body, so treat it as an inexpensive second vacuum. Next to the Compact it has a longer wand but fewer floor features.

Clear hair from the roll, wipe the sole and wheels and empty the cup. Avoid dropping it, since a budget plastic body cracks. The wand is the reason to own it: it reaches cobwebs, curtain tops and ceiling corners, but a long wand adds weight at the end of the arm, so rest the body on the floor while you use it. Keep the wand's release latch free of lint, because a latch that does not seat leaves a gap in the airflow and the tool seems dead, and store the wand clipped to the body so it does not bend.
products.bestFor: Small homes that want a cheap light upright with a long wand.

products.name: Amazon Basics bagless upright, washable filter, 1.7L cup
products.description:
The Amazon Basics upright is the baseline: a corded bagless machine with a washable filter, a 1.7 liter cup and crevice and upholstery tools. Corded power means no battery limits across a whole session.

It is the cheapest machine in the group and has the fewest features. Compared with the NEU182B it has a smaller cup and no height adjustment listed, but it covers basic cleaning of carpet and hard floors.

Wash the filter and let it dry for a full day, empty the cup before it fills and check the roll for hair. Treat it as a low-cost tool that you replace when it wears out. A washable filter only saves money if you let it dry completely, so own a spare and swap them, since a damp filter in a closed housing grows a musty smell. Because the listing is a house brand, keep the receipt and the model number in a folder, and check that the filter is sold separately before you buy, since a vacuum with no replacement parts is a vacuum with a fixed lifespan.
products.bestFor: Basic cleaning on a very tight budget.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Airspeed NEU10AE4 is about 7.7 pounds, the Bissell Compact under 8 and the NEU182B about 10. At this price a light body is the main selling point. A machine you can lift gets used, so pick the lightest that has the features you need, and remember that a very light head floats on a deep rug instead of pressing into it, so test your choice against the carpet you clean most often and not against the stairs you climb once a week.

The NEU182B has a 2.6 liter cup and the Amazon Basics 1.7 liters, while compact models have smaller tanks. A small cup forces frequent stops. Match the cup to your home, and note that a larger cup is heavier when full, so a household that wants a light machine should empty it more often, while a house with a shedding dog and a lot of carpet should prefer the bigger cup despite the weight.

Budget uprights use plain rolls, which wrap long hair. A multi-floor roll like the Dirt Devil's helps on mixed surfaces. Check the roll every few weeks and keep scissors nearby, because a wrapped roll stops spinning, pushes dirt around and heats the belt, and at this price a snapped belt is the most common reason a machine is thrown away when a two-minute repair would have saved it.
The Amazon Basics lists a washable filter, and others use foam and felt filters. A clogged filter cuts suction. Wash it monthly and let it dry for a full day.
The NEU182B has five height settings. A head too low drags on a rug and too high leaves dirt. Look for a height control if your home has mixed floors.

Under $100 you do not get a sealed housing, a pod or a roll that adapts to the floor. For allergies or thick carpet, step up a tier. Be honest about the job: weekly cleaning on low pile and hard floors. If you can foresee needing a sealed filter or a pod within a year, it is cheaper to buy the better machine once than a budget one twice, since a failed belt or cracked housing in year two erases most of the savings.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter cuts airflow. Dry fully.
Hair wraps the roll and strains the belt. Cut it free with scissors over a bin, and spin the roll by hand afterward to confirm that it turns freely.
A worn belt stops the roll and the machine then pushes dirt around. A belt is a cheap part, so replace it at the first sign of slipping and keep a spare with the manual.

faq.q: Is a vacuum under $100 any good?
faq.a: For weekly cleaning on low pile and hard floors, yes. Thick carpet and allergies need a higher tier, because the brush, the housing seal and the motor are the parts a budget maker economizes on, and no amount of marketing wattage replaces them. Think of these machines as reliable weekly cleaners rather than deep-cleaning tools.

faq.q: Does the $100 cap reflect current prices?
faq.a: We checked the listings on the update date; a machine can slip above the cap later, so confirm the live price before you order.
The Eureka NEU182B with 2.6 liters, which is large for this class. The Amazon Basics follows with 1.7 liters, and the compact models have smaller tanks that need emptying after each session.

Yes, plain rolls do, especially with long human or pet hair. Check the roll every few weeks, cut the strands free with scissors and spin the roll by hand to confirm that it turns freely before you start again.

Several years with a new belt now and then. Plastic bodies are not rugged, so the usual end of life is a cracked housing or a burnt motor after a long run with a clogged filter, both of which are avoided by regular emptying and washing.

Not at this price. Wash the filters and empty the cup outdoors, into a bag held tight to the opening, because a bagless cup releases a puff of fine dust at the moment it opens and a basic filter will not catch the finest particles. Households with asthma should treat these machines as general cleaners and look a tier higher for a sealed system.
